# requireScalar

<link-summary>Returns the value as a scalar, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireScalar() — Returns the value as a scalar, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireScalar(
  value: unknown,
  message: string = "Expected a scalar value."
): string | number | boolean | symbol | bigint;
```

A primitive that carries a single value: string, number, boolean, symbol or bigint. `null` and `undefined` are primitives too, but they carry no value and do not qualify.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                             | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :---------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                               | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a scalar value."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`string | number | boolean | symbol | bigint` — the same value, typed as a scalar.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                  |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a scalar. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireScalar("abc"); // => "abc"
requireScalar(1); // => 1
requireScalar({}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireScalar([]); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
